significance.justification: Verified true, the primary conclusion would be that the student’s “RELATIONAL structure (value covariance/graph) transmits” so that its graph preferentially resembles its own teacher’s beyond independent value shifts; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling, while the proposed “low-dimensional early-layer value subspace whose ablation collapses the configuration jointly” adds a form-(ii) causal mechanism. The phenomenon would constrain expectations for untested value profiles—configuration-level inheritance rather than independently transmitted marginals—and the mechanism would explain why several value behaviors move or collapse together, a materially stronger conclusion than the scalar preference and misalignment transmission reported in Cloud et al.’s 2025 Subliminal Learning work. The branches are determinate: preservation of teacher-specific covariance supports structured transmission, whereas transferred levels without geometry rules it out within the stated matched-base setting and establishes a scalar-like bandwidth boundary; total failure would be less informative but would still reject the bundled hypothesis in scope. Topic-substitution check: merely restating “extend subliminal learning” would not justify this score; the graph-level coupling, valence-dependent fidelity relation, and joint causal subspace are the claim-specific reasons it sits above the topic median.

reach.justification: The clearest downstream handle is the design rule that “value-audits should test the relational profile (not just individual value levels),” supplemented by the proposed intervention target, a “low-dimensional early-layer value subspace” whose ablation jointly removes the configuration. The audit is ex ante with respect to deployment—it can gate a distilled model before shipping, although it is post-training—and thus could be used by distillation auditors and deployment practitioners rather than only by researchers explaining an observed failure. After per-model re-extraction, the graph claim still predicts a relation—greater student similarity to its own teacher and potentially higher prosocial than antisocial fidelity—whereas the particular activation subspace itself must be rediscovered; the asserted scope covers matched-base subliminal transfer across multiple values and carriers, but does not itself establish the stated model-merging risk or a universal cross-architecture law. Topic-substitution check: the general subliminal-learning topic supplies no comparable audit or forecast, so the relational-profile screen, its pre-shipping action window, and the transferable teacher–student coupling support the above-median reach.
